the mean of the variable above x

items.q: A p value reports

the probability that the null hypothesis is true
the probability that the alternative is true
items.s: The p value is computed under the null hypothesis; it is not the probability that the null is true.

items.q: A confidence interval is preferred to a bare point estimate because it

items.s: A point estimate alone hides its precision; an interval conveys the likely range.

the probability of rejecting the null hypothesis when it is false
the probability that the null is true

items.s: Type one error is rejection of a true null, controlled by the significance level.

items.q: The binomial distribution applies when

each trial has two outcomes and the trials are independent
items.s: Binomial conditions: fixed number of trials, two outcomes per trial, constant probability, independent trials.

a single value used to estimate a parameter
items.s: A point estimate is one number; an interval estimate adds a margin of error.

items.q: Increasing the sample size, with everything else fixed, makes a confidence interval

o: the statement of no effect or no difference

items.s: The null states no effect; the alternative states the effect being sought.

items.q: A two tailed test is used when

items.s: Two tailed testing splits the significance level between both tails when no direction is claimed.

items.q: Lowering the significance level from five to one per cent makes a type one error
items.s: The significance level is the probability of a type one error, so reducing it reduces that risk.

items.q: The critical value of a test depends on

the number of variables in the data set only
items.s: Critical values come from the chosen distribution at the chosen significance level.

items.q: A chi square statistic close to zero suggests
o: observed and expected frequencies agree well

the strength of the linear relation
items.s: The slope is the rate of change of the fitted y with respect to x.
